inputs.original_text: More tenancies mean little if people are still ending up in emergency accommodation and families are worried about eviction. Micheál Martin can point to lease figures, but security is what matters. Forcing landlords into six-year leases from March 1 may sound compassionate, yet piling on rules risks driving ordinary providers out and leaving renters with fewer options. Government should focus on stable homes for families, not headline numbers and policies that make the housing market harder to navigate.
inputs.modified_text: Families need dependable homes, not government spin about lease figures. Micheál Martin may point to more tenancies, but that means little when people still face emergency accommodation or fear eviction. Forcing landlords into six-year leases from March 1 risks driving ordinary providers away and shrinking choices for renters. A housing policy that makes it harder to provide homes is no help to families; government should put stability and responsibility ahead of headline numbers and more rules.
